_readme: Allowlist for tools/check-backlog-citations.mjs. Every key is a (BL|BUG|DEBT)-N id cited somewhere in tracked source that does NOT resolve via `backlog get-item --repo sox-ecosystem --human-id <id>`. Each entry's `reason` records WHY that's expected/acceptable rather than a defect, so this file stays a legible audit trail and not a growing pile of silenced red. Compiled 2026-08-18 remediating DEBT-006. `cause` is one of: PLAN_LOCAL_BUG014 (docs/plan/bug014-store-hardening/SPEC.md T1-T11 own numbering colliding with the graph's BUG/DEBT families), PLAN_LOCAL_RUNTIME_PROD (a SECOND, independently-discovered collision: docs/plan/runtime-productionization/ has its own BL-1xx work-package numbering that collides with the graph's real BL family — NOT part of DEBT-006's original diagnosis, found during this remediation, not yet disambiguated at the source because that plan is outside this packet's scope), MIGRATION_DROPPED (existed as a real heading in BACKLOG.md history pre-2026-08-06 migration, never carried into the graph), STILL_LOST (existed briefly during the 2026-08-14 backlog data-loss incident, explicitly recorded in HANDOFF-20260814.md §C as unrecoverable from any transcript), NOT_A_CITATION (the regex matched prose/example/fixture content that was never intended as a real backlog reference), or SUPERSEDED_BY_NEW_FILING (this remediation filed a real graph item for the underlying work; a residual bare mention of the old placeholder id remains in a historical narrative string).

Left as (a) allowlisted pending that decision — see DEBT-006 remediation notes.
